# AI-generated inserts

Use one or two where type and shapes
cannot carry the idea on their own, not in every beat.

Keep one short shared style description (material, palette from the brand kit,
lighting) and reuse it in every insert prompt.

## Transparent inserts

Video models return opaque frames, so produce the subject on a flat key color
and key it out:

1. **Still.** With [make-image](../../make-image/SKILL.md), generate the element
   alone, centered with margin, on a flat, evenly lit pure green (`#00FF00`)
   background with no cast shadow on the ground. Use magenta (`#FF00FF`) when the
   subject itself is green.
2. **Animate.** With [make-ai-video](../../make-ai-video/SKILL.md), use its default
   image-to-video model with that still. Ask for a locked-off
   static camera, the subject staying fully in frame, one clear action, and a
   background that stays the same flat color throughout. Write it in that model's
   syntax ([model prompting](../../make-ai-video/references/model-prompting.md)) and
   generate no audio where the model has the switch; the insert's sound is designed
   separately.
3. **Key.** Use the bundled `ffmpeg`:

   ```sh
   ffmpeg -i insert.mp4 -vf "chromakey=0x00FF00:0.15:0.05,despill=type=green,format=yuva444p10le" \
     -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 4444 -pix_fmt yuva444p10le insert.mov
   ffmpeg -i insert.mp4 -vf "chromakey=0x00FF00:0.15:0.05,despill=type=green,format=yuva420p" \
     -c:v libvpx-vp9 -pix_fmt yuva420p -b:v 0 -crf 30 insert.webm
   ```

   For a magenta key use `0xFF00FF` and drop `despill`. Use ProRes 4444 for After
   Effects and editors, and WebM VP9 for Remotion or HyperFrames.

When the insert sits on a flat panel that does not move, generating directly on
that panel's exact color can skip keying. A moving background needs the key.

## In the composition

Hand the insert to the motif of the next beat.

# Color and brand

For any named brand, logo, brand kit or requested brand match, and for color contrast.

## Core

- Real brand facts win over inferred treatment. Use the selected snapshot's
  palette, type and supplied logo files, unmodified and in their documented
  variants.
- Exceptions are recorded, not improvised: they live in the brand snapshot's
  `overrides.md` or the active design direction.
- Say what was substituted or unavailable instead of claiming full brand
  fidelity, and name the kit used in the handoff.

## Using a kit

Read the project's brand snapshot (normally `brand/BRAND.md`, with `kit.json`
for tokens and the guides it links) as the `brand-kit` skill describes, and only
the fields the deliverable needs. Work for a website reads its site kit,
`brand/sites/<host>/kit.md`: take colours from `palette.json`, load the faces in
`fonts/` as local fonts, and place logos from `logos/` in the variant `kit.md`
marks transparent.

## Logos and marks

Inspect a logo file before placing it: pick the variant that suits the ground.
Verify a downloaded official mark against its published hash when one is given.
Partner and platform marks are sourced separately and never replace the user's
own brand as the design's identity.

## Color and contrast

A gradient word must stay readable at every stop; on
a dark ground, end on the lightest accent, never on dark purple, navy or black.

## After compression

Judge color in the encoded file, not the composition: faint decoration (glows,
patterns, watermark shapes) can vanish once encoded.

# Locate and safe areas

For placing labels, callouts and boxes on real images or moving subjects, and platform safe areas.

## Core

- Keep essential text and marks inside the platform's safe area (the `make-ai-video` skill's `references/social-safe-areas.md` lists them).

## Locate before you annotate

Before placing a callout,
ring or label on a real image, get a box for the target, draw it, and look:

- **Segment it.** `voyager media cutout FRAME --prompt "the red car" --output
  located.png` (SAM 3, metered, about half a cent) keeps every confident match,
  so name exactly one instance ("the left-most car"). Then `voyager media
  crop-alpha located.png --output crop.png --json` reports its `box` (x, y,
  width, height in frame pixels) at no cost.
- **Otherwise,** crop and zoom progressively, then map back to frame coordinates.

## Labels on moving subjects

Anchor labels to the actual subject. Check the moving intervals,
not one still, and keep leader endpoints on the named part.

# Rights and delivery

For asset rights, credits, subtitles and delivery checks.

## Core

- Deliver a `CREDITS` file naming every third-party asset (samples, music, fonts, images, the voice engine) with its source and licence; credit on screen where a licence requires it; tell the user `CREDITS` lists the licences and the material is their responsibility.
- When anything is spoken, offer an `.srt` in one line.
- `voyager media review FILE` measures loudness but flags only a true peak above 0 dBTP (clipping): check `audio.integratedLUFS` near −14 and `audio.truePeakDBTP` at or below −1 yourself. It also checks black frames and duration. Re-level with two-pass `loudnorm` (`TP=-1`, `linear=true`, the first pass's measured values) and review again before presenting.
- To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use a video-understanding model with `voyager models run`; load `choose-media-model/references/understanding.md` for the paid upload route.

# Illustrative motion

For requests to animate a drawing, logo, pattern, ink or line art, or a brand
element, where the ask is to bring that artwork itself to life. A brand mark
carried as a motif through a promo still morphs and hands off as the skill
describes; this reference governs how the art forms. The failure mode is to
leave the finished art intact and move it: spin it, drift it, orbit it, or
reveal a raster behind a wipe. The user wants the artwork to be drawn in motion,
with the movement happening inside the drawing.

## Fidelity first

User-supplied art is the source of truth. Restore it; do not reinterpret it.
Clean up with a reference-guided edit that keeps every stroke where it is (an
image edit such as Nano Banana asked only to clean the ink), or pull parts
directly from the pixels or components of the original. Do not add procedural
extensions, new geometry, extra flourishes or a "more dynamic" redraw. Make
variations only when the user asks for them.

## Pipeline

1. **Clean up**: pure ink on transparency, with no bloom, smudge or paper texture.
2. **Vectorize** the cleaned art, then reduce each stroke to a **centerline with a
   width at every point**: store points as `[x, y, halfWidth]`.
3. **Order the strokes as a tree.** Each stroke records its `parent` and the
   `attach` position (0–1) along the parent where it sprouts, plus `start` and
   `duration`. A child is placed at its parent's current attach point, so it
   grows out of the ink already drawn and never floats in.
4. **Draw with taper**: the outline of the centerline drawn so far, at its
   per-point width, with a rounded cap at the growing tip. A small curl that
   relaxes to zero as the stroke completes (unfurling) adds life without
   changing the final shape. Do not render a stroke before its `start`: at
   progress 0 a rounded cap still paints a dot at its origin.

For uniform-width line art (monoline logos, diagrams), `@remotion/paths` is
enough: `evolvePath(progress, d)` returns the `strokeDasharray` and
`strokeDashoffset` for a draw-on with `strokeLinecap="round"` (again, skip
strokes that have not started, or their caps show as dots). For tapered ink,
use its `getLength`, `getPointAtLength` and `getTangentAtLength` to sample the
centerline and normals, and draw the outline yourself. The package is not in the
default project pins; add `@remotion/paths` at the pinned Remotion version, as
[edit-in-remotion](../../edit-in-remotion/SKILL.md) describes.

**Raster-only art** (too dense or textured to vectorize faithfully): build a
geodesic **arrival map** from the cleaned art. Take the largest connected ink
component, pick a seed at the drawing's natural origin (stem base, pen start),
and run Dijkstra *through the ink pixels only*. Each detached component starts when the nearest
main-ink point arrives, then propagates from its own nearest pixel. Give
antialiased fringe and background pixels the value of their nearest ink pixel,
so soft edges reveal with their stroke.

In Remotion, reveal the cleaned art through a luminance `<mask>` made from that
map, thresholded at the current progress: `feComponentTransfer` on `feFuncR`,
`feFuncG` and `feFuncB` (not `feFuncA`) with slope `-1/softness` and intercept
`progress/softness`, and `color-interpolation-filters="sRGB"`. Animate `progress` from 0 to
`1 + softness`, not to 1; at 1 the latest-arriving tips are still partly hidden.
The final frame is then the cleaned art, pixel for pixel.

Do not reveal art with wide mask strokes (hundreds of pixels over thin ink), an
expanding circle or a linear wipe.

## Form, don't transform

For artwork, "alive" means the art itself is growing. Do not rotate, drift, scale-pulse or
orbit finished art to keep the frame moving. Secondary life comes from the
formation: overlapping strokes, a tip still unfurling while the next branch
starts. Once formed, the art holds still within the frame. A slow camera push
over the whole frame, drawing included, is fine; moving the drawing on its own
against its surroundings is not.

## Timing

Stagger along the drawing's topology, from root outwards, trunk before branches,
overlapping so that several tips grow at once.

## Combining motifs

Put motifs together only when they connect: one grows out of another, a line
from one becomes the stem of the next. Never collage unrelated drawings in one
frame, or cut between them without a handoff.

## Quality bar

Every intermediate frame's ink lies within the final frame's ink, apart from a
relaxing unfurl curl, and the final frame matches the approved still.

# Motion that explains an event

Use when authoring counts, diagrams, tracked labels or explanatory animation.

Rendering a frame must not depend on which frame rendered first; that includes SVG def ids. A demonstration can use deliberately chosen examples for legibility, but do not present those as an unbiased sample.

Anchor labels to the actual subject as [locate and safe areas](craft/locate-and-safe-areas.md) describes.

Read [caption craft](../../edit-video/references/caption-craft.md) when authoring speech text.

# Music sync: cutting picture to a track

Read when the user supplies a song or bed and the picture is cut to it: a lyric
video, a music-driven promo, a montage. Scoring music to a finished picture is the
reverse job: [make-music](../../make-music/SKILL.md); hits and risers:
[make-sound](../../make-sound/SKILL.md).

## Lock the grid first

Measure the track before planning beats. Voyager bundles FFmpeg but no beat tracker, so measure with
librosa in a throwaway environment (needs network once; without `uv`, use a
temporary `python3 -m venv` outside the project, never the system Python). The script mixes to mono, so check a stereo track for phase
inversion first and analyse one channel if needed (see
[measure the reference](../../make-ai-video/references/reference-video.md)). This script prints the
tempo, beat and onset times, and the two numbers that decide whether to trust the
grid:

```python
# grid.py: uv run --no-project --with librosa python3 grid.py song.wav
import json, sys
import librosa, numpy as np

y, sr = librosa.load(sys.argv[1], sr=22050, mono=True)
env = librosa.onset.onset_strength(y=y, sr=sr)
tempo, frames = librosa.beat.beat_track(onset_envelope=env, sr=sr)
beats = librosa.frames_to_time(frames, sr=sr)
onsets = librosa.onset.onset_detect(onset_envelope=env, sr=sr, units="time")
between = (frames[:-1] + frames[1:]) // 2
gaps = np.diff(beats)
rms = librosa.feature.rms(y=y)[0]
print(json.dumps({
    "tempo": round(float(np.atleast_1d(tempo)[0]), 1),
    "beats": [round(float(t), 3) for t in beats],
    "onsets": [round(float(t), 3) for t in onsets],
    "beatContrast": round(min(99.0, float(env[frames].mean() / (env[between].mean() + 1e-9))), 1) if len(between) else None,
    "beatSpread": round(float(gaps.std() / gaps.mean()), 3) if len(gaps) > 1 else None,
    "energyPerSecond": [round(float(v), 4) for v in rms[:: sr // 512]],
}))
```

Run it per section on a long track (trim with FFmpeg `-ss`/`-t` first), since
trust can change between a verse and a chorus. librosa gives beats, not bars:
take the downbeat as the beat where section changes, energy jumps and the
strongest onsets fall (ask the user when it stays unclear), and count bars of
four from it.

## Decide what to trust

A beat tracker always returns a grid. On calm or sparse music it invents a
metronome, often at double the real pulse, that sits on no audible hit. Trust the
grid in a section only when it lands on accents and holds steady: `beatContrast`
(onset strength on the beats against halfway between them) clearly above 1, as a
rough guide 2 or more, and `beatSpread` a few percent. Near 1 the grid is
imposed; pace that section by phrases and energy instead. A tempo above about 140
on music that feels unhurried is usually double time: halve it. Decide per
section:

- **Beat cut**: the grid is real. Hard cuts and per-onset reveals anchor to beats.
- **Phrase flow**: the grid is doubtful or the music is calm. Moves span whole
  phrases (a slow push, a crossfade); no per-onset cuts.

# Narrated explainer

For a narrated concept explainer built as designed motion: how DNS resolves a
name, what a rebase does, how a product works under the hood. Equations,
algorithms and scientific relationships stay with
[edit-in-manim](../../edit-in-manim/SKILL.md). The promotional treatment does not
apply here. The narration carries the argument, and every picture is timed to the word that
introduces it.

## Order of work

1. **Script.** Check `voyager voice agent capabilities` `narration` first; when narration is
   unavailable, on-screen text carries the script (captions-led, as
   [voiceover](../../voiceover/SKILL.md) describes). Write it in full in your reply. With
   narration available, record it next and show the script beside the take; whether to
   ask first follows [voiceover](../../voiceover/SKILL.md)'s step 6, so never when the user
   said to proceed or asked for a finished draft. When you do ask, save the script with
   `voyager voice agent production_update` first: the chat and the question card preview
   it. A script only in a file is one the user never sees.
2. **Voice take.** Record it as one take with [voiceover](../../voiceover/SKILL.md)
   and get the take approved, or approve it yourself when they said to proceed or asked
   for a finished draft.
3. **Cue sheet** from the approved take's word timings (below).
4. **Plan the pictures** against the cue sheet: the storyboard's beats are the
   scenes, each card naming its cue words and what appears on each. Rough style
   frames can come earlier, alongside the script, to settle the look; the timed
   storyboard waits for the cue sheet.
5. **Motion test, then build.** Render a 2–4 s motion test, present it with
   `voyager files present PATH --deliverable none --json` with a one-line progress
   note that does not embed it (chat shows each as a card), and keep building without waiting for a reply.

A script change after step 2 means a new take or a repair, then a regenerated cue
sheet, never hand-shifted times.

## Script

Write it by voiceover's [writing for the ear](../../voiceover/references/direction.md#writing-for-the-ear)
rules.

## Cue sheet

`voyager voice agent take {takeId}` on the approved take gives `alignment` and, when that is
`complete` or `partial`, `transcriptPath`: a speech transcript whose `words` each
carry an `id` (`word_` plus 24 hex characters), the written `text`, and `startUs`
and `endUs` in microseconds. With `alignment` `mismatch` or `none` there are no
word timings; fix the take first ([takes and
repairs](../../voiceover/references/takes-and-repairs.md)).

Build a table from it, one row per picture change and at least one per sentence:
beat, sentence, cue word, its word `id`, `startUs`, and the visual event. Save it
as a JSON or CSV file in the project and have the composition read its times
from that file (frame = `startUs` ÷ 1,000,000 × fps), never from hand-typed
seconds, so a repair or retake only means regenerating the table.

- A word spoken twice is two rows with different `id`s; pick the occurrence by
  `id`, never by its text.
- Check cue words with apostrophes, numbers and respelled names against the
  transcript's `text` before trusting a text match.

**Growing one diagram.** When several scenes build the same diagram, keep one
table of positions for all of them, start each scene with the earlier parts
already on screen, and change scenes inside the diagram with a cut or a fade,
not a slide or push.

## Voice track

Play the approved take as one continuous `<Audio>` and time every picture to it
from the cue sheet. Never split a take into per-line `<Audio>` sequences, and
never pad or trim segment lengths to space the lines: provider word timings end
late in each pause and start after the real onset, so a cut between two lines
leaves a fragment of the next word and clips its start ("It– It runs"). To give a
line more or less room, change that pause with `voyager voice agent repair {kind: "pause"}`
([exact pauses](../../voiceover/references/takes-and-repairs.md#exact-pauses)),
approve the edited take and regenerate the cue sheet.

In render QA, when any voice audio is cut, run `voyager speech splices` on the
take with the trims the composition plays, in seconds of the take, and fix every
flag before presenting:

```sh
voyager speech splices voice/take.mp3 --segments '[{"start":0,"end":7.72},{"start":7.72,"end":11.07}]' --json
```

## Motion

No ambient loops (breathe, float, glow pulse) and no slow push or pan added to the back half of a held read. Once a
reveal has resolved, a still hold while the narration finishes is correct; a freeze
while the narration is still naming new things is a front-loaded beat to fix.
Product UI beats use the cursor in [product UI](product-ui.md#composed-cursor).

# Product UI in motion

When a scene must match an existing product UI, inspect a visual reference and
its corresponding current source before reconstructing it. Label the reference's
surface/version: marketing pages, external integration demos and historical
recordings can show a different interface. Reconstruct only the needed
presentation components rather than booting or importing the whole product.
Use crops to focus attention instead of silently removing known controls from
a full UI view.

## Composed cursor

For a cursor drawn into composed or rebuilt UI. A recorded demo keeps its real
pointer from [screen capture](../../screen-capture/SKILL.md); do not restage it
with these rules.

- **Entry.** From off-screen, on one continuous vector, decelerating onto its
  first target. Never fade or mask it in at rest.
- **Click.** The target reacts in its own tween on the same frame; a click that
  only focuses a field gets no target reaction.
- **The click starts the next beat.** A morph, a typing run or a panel opening
  is caused by a click, never simply begins.
- **Lead the move.** Start the travel before the click, so the click lands on its
  spoken word or musical accent. Put no clicks in the incoming transition window.
- **Off duty.** During a beat it does not own (typing, narration), it drifts
  aside rather than sitting on the action or idling.
- **Exit.** Accelerate off the nearest edge, or just before a cut start toward the next scene's first click point; the next
  scene picks it up at that pose and decelerates at the same speed. Never fade it out in place.

## Promotional motion treatment

Good promotional motion feels like one continuous picture:

- **Constant motion.** Nothing freezes, holds included, apart from the brief
  stillness before the climax. When text must sit to be read, a camera push continues toward its destination, an
  asset keeps its slow push (Ken Burns), or the next piece stages in. Pause
  anywhere and something meaningful is mid-flight; ambient breathe, float or
  glow loops never stand in for it. Artwork the user asks to have drawn in motion is the
  exception: a drawing, logo or pattern stays alive by forming, not by spinning
  or drifting once finished (see
  [illustrative motion](illustrative-motion.md)). A mark used as a
  motif still transforms as below.
- **Motifs that carry and transform.** A shape, mark or character persists across
  beats and becomes the next thing: a logo unfolds into a figure that acts, which
  then splits into the three points of the next beat. When the project has
  approved artwork, build the motif from it (recombine, crop, re-time or extend
  it); otherwise invent one for this piece. The example is only an example. No
  cuts or fades between unrelated screens.
- **Kinetic typography with variety.** Type is the main image, not a caption.
  Use a different reveal technique in each beat.
- **The message leads.** In a product or brand intro, every beat puts new words
  on screen (UI labels and captions in a product shot count), and once the
  previous copy has had its readable hold, no long stretch runs on graphics
  alone. The final lockup and its end hold are exempt.
  "Constant motion" above supports the copy and never replaces it. When a brief
  asks for both more product detail and richer graphics, the detail gets the
  screen time.
- **Compositions that break the grid.** Asymmetry, overscaled type, elements
  bleeding off frame, depth layers moving at different rates. Avoid a centered
  title over a card grid beat after beat.
- **Mixed media.** A short AI-generated clip can bring a beat to life, even in a
  pure motion-graphics explainer: for example, a claymation figure acting out the
  idea on a transparent background beside the text. See
  [AI inserts](ai-inserts.md) for generation and keying.
- **Real subjects.** Open image sources are listed in
  [image sources](image-sources.json) (Servier Medical Art and NIH BioArt for
  medicine and biology, Wikimedia Commons for diagrams, photos and maps). A
  sourced illustration can still be traced, recolored or split into layers to
  animate. Record its page, license and credit in the project, and credit it in
  the piece when the license requires.

When the picture is cut to a supplied song or music bed, read
[music sync](music-sync.md). For explanatory counts, diagrams,
anchored labels or loops, also read [meaningful motion](meaningful-motion.md). When a scene must
match a real product UI, read [product UI](product-ui.md). When the ask
is to animate a drawing, logo, pattern, ink or line art, or a brand element, read
[illustrative motion](illustrative-motion.md) first.

Unless the user named or saved a motion tool, build in
[Remotion](../edit-in-remotion/SKILL.md), then [HyperFrames](../edit-in-hyperframes/SKILL.md).
[fframes](../edit-in-fframes/SKILL.md) renders Rust and SVG with Skia and linked libav; its toolchain is not bundled.
[EffectCraft](../edit-in-effectcraft/SKILL.md) supports editable compositions, Lottie and transparent video; its CLI is not bundled.
[Tesseract](../edit-in-tesseract/SKILL.md) edits layered `.tsrct` projects through Mirage's standalone CLI.
Use [After Effects](../edit-in-after-effects/SKILL.md) only when the user names it,
the project already uses it, or they ask for an After Effects project file. Set up through the tool's
integration skill, not upstream `npx`. Revise an existing native project in its
own editor.

For a named brand or product, take its logo, colors and typefaces from its site
with [brand-kit](../brand-kit/SKILL.md) (`voyager brand site --url URL --json`)
before designing.
From an article or page, work from its full text (fetch the page itself, not a
summary); keep every on-screen claim to one of its sentences with its qualifiers
(preview, beta, plan, dates), and point the CTA at that page's URL.
Write English copy in US spelling unless the user, their brand kit or the project uses another variety.

## Design like a motion designer

Think like a top motion designer making something people will remember.
Find one idea for the piece, and let every choice carry that idea through time.

**Avoid slideshow design.** Use interesting layouts and vary them between beats
and scenes; use a different kind of kinetic typography from scene to scene. Keep something
moving; no frozen holds before the end card.

**In short-form social, viral and ads, hook the viewer in the first 1–3 seconds.** That video has sharp drop-off; don't waste a frame. A narrative or slow-burn piece can take its time. Keep strobes and full-frame flashes under 3 per second (WCAG).

**Cut at the brand's pace.** With a brand's captured motion (`brand/motion.json`), the shots come
from the edit-in skill's brand-motion helper (`shotFrames` in Remotion, `windows` in HyperFrames),
not from the copy: one line can span several shots, and every cut changes the frame. The brand's
title entrance then replaces scene-to-scene variety in type entrances (a punch-in brand's
titles show small, then hard-cut to the same words much larger); vary layout, scale and
framing instead.

**Use motifs.** Give the piece visual elements that survive from beat to beat
or scene to scene, or show up in several places, so it reads as one story.
Contrast works: balance consistency with variety. A project's approved artwork
is where new graphics start, even when the user loosens how exactly to use it.

**Aim to wow.** Where it suits the piece, add a flourish that signals high-end
work: particles, real 3D depth, light and glow, a camera move through space.

## Routing and assembly

Equations, algorithms and scientific relationships start in
[edit-in-manim](../edit-in-manim/SKILL.md); narrated concept explainers follow
[narrated explainer](references/narrated-explainer.md); seamless loops and GIFs
use [make-social-loop](../make-social-loop/SKILL.md); milestone-number reveals
use [make-announcement-video](../make-announcement-video/SKILL.md).

An existing Resolve or Premiere edit, or one the user asked to finish in an
editor, is not converted or replaced: render the motion elements and bring them
in through [edit-in-resolve](../edit-in-resolve/SKILL.md) or
[edit-in-premiere](../edit-in-premiere/SKILL.md). When the user wants them built
natively in Resolve, edit-in-resolve builds them as Fusion nodes and keyframes
there, the free edition included; Voyager's bundled
FFmpeg only when no editor was named (no `libx264`: macOS
`-c:v h264_videotoolbox -q:v 85`, Windows `-c:v h264_mf -b:v 12M`,
[others](../make-social-loop/references/delivery.md#bundled-ffmpeg-encoders); not a
system `ffmpeg`). For recordings, read
`capture.json` for track paths and timing. [edit-video](../edit-video/SKILL.md)
owns transcripts, word timing and plain captions; designed or kinetic captions
built from those timings are made here.

In Remotion, preview with a standalone HTML export presented with
`voyager files present PATH --deliverable none`; the user can comment on it in
the Files pane. Every move, push-in and zoom follows edit-in-remotion's
[smooth motion](../edit-in-remotion/SKILL.md#smooth-motion) rules: in a slow
zoom, a live-text UI panel can micro-jitter where an image of it does not.
Before presenting a render, check every cut and transition frame by frame with
edit-in-remotion's [transition strips](../edit-in-remotion/SKILL.md#review-the-render),
and fix stray exit elements, unintended overlaps and one-frame glitches.

A launch film or promo built from real product screens follows make-product-demo's
[look check](../make-product-demo/SKILL.md#look-before-building-the-cut): render
stills and a short range, open them yourself and fix them before the full render.
Every composed piece presents its first style frame and a 2–4 s motion test with
`--deliverable none` as soon as they exist, with a one-line progress note that does not embed it (chat shows each as a card), then keeps
building without waiting for a reply.

For continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use [watch and listen](../choose-media-model/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).
